research_question: What is the effect of LigaSure haemorrhoidectomy, compared with conventional diathermy haemorrhoidectomy, on operating time (minutes) in adults with symptomatic haemorrhoids?
outcome_description: Operating time measured in minutes from the start of the surgical excision to wound closure/hemostasis completion.
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates longer operating time in the LigaSure group compared to the conventional diathermy group; a negative effect size indicates shorter operating time with LigaSure.
search_queries: LigaSure conventional diathermy haemorrhoidectomy operating time trial
LigaSure diathermy hemorrhoidectomy operative time comparison quantitative
bipolar vessel sealing diathermy hemorrhoidectomy controlled trial
inclusion_criteria: Adult patients undergoing surgical excision for symptomatic haemorrhoids
Direct comparison between LigaSure (electrothermal vessel sealing) haemorrhoidectomy and conventional diathermy (electrosurgical) haemorrhoidectomy
Reports quantitative outcome data on operating duration/time in minutes
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, letters, commentaries, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between LigaSure haemorrhoidectomy and conventional diathermy haemorrhoidectomy
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size (e.g., missing mean/SD, median/range/IQR, or test statistics for operating time)
Completely unrelated to surgical management of haemorrhoids
moderators_to_extract: Study design (randomised controlled trial vs non-randomised comparative study)
Haemorrhoidectomy surgical technique (open Milligan-Morgan vs closed Ferguson)
Haemorrhoid grade/severity (e.g., Grade III vs Grade IV)
